title: Beta-blockers and inhibitors of the renin-angiotensin aldosterone system for chronic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
authors: Martin N, Manoharan K, Davies C, Lumbers RT
population: 41 randomised trials in adults with heart failure and left ventricular ejection fraction above 40%; ACE inhibitors 8 trials (2061 participants, mean ages 70 to 82), angiotensin receptor blockers 8 trials (8755 participants); search to 14 May 2020
funder: not read: the full-text record in Europe PMC returned the abstract and results text without the sources-of-support section, and the Cochrane Library page is not accessible.
result: ACE inhibitors, moderate certainty: cardiovascular mortality RR 0.93 (95% CI 0.61 to 1.42; 945 participants), all-cause mortality 1.04 (0.75 to 1.45; 1187) and heart-failure hospitalisation 0.86 (0.64 to 1.15; 1019); effects on hyperkalaemia uncertain. Angiotensin receptor blockers, high certainty: cardiovascular mortality 1.02 (0.90 to 1.14; 7254), all-cause mortality 1.01 (0.92 to 1.11; 7964), heart-failure hospitalisation 0.92 (0.83 to 1.02), and hyperkalaemia 1.88 (1.07 to 3.33; 7148). The authors conclude that current evidence does not support ACE inhibitors or angiotensin receptor blockers in this condition without another indication.
